scope: Issuing business/product operations; US baseline with explicit UK complaint comparison.

evidence_status_definition.documented: The bounded public Amex behavior described in normal_flow is documented; this does not imply every exception or authenticated screen was observed.
evidence_status_definition.partial: Only part of the business journey is established, a regional comparison is required, or current interactive evidence is limited.
evidence_status_definition.gap: No sufficient public evidence for the specified Amex business behavior.

field_interpretation.normal_flow: Short public-evidence summary. Earlier sources are referenced without reproducing their full study.
field_interpretation.exceptions: Observed limitations, unresolved details and business distinctions to review.
field_interpretation.account_control_handoff: Proposed Etail responsibility and visibility review unless explicitly stated otherwise.
field_interpretation.merchant_handoff: Proposed Etail cross-party review unless explicitly stated otherwise.
field_interpretation.etail_gap: Design/inventory gap or deliberate difference; not a code audit or implementation score.
field_interpretation.acceptance_scenario: Proposed fictional business walkthrough, not an executed test.
field_interpretation.comparison_ids: Related rows in the unchanged 90-task comparison inventory. A link is not a full-coverage or pass claim; [] means a distinct journey is absent.

checks.journey: Choose a product and understand the offer
normal_flow: Indexed US shopping copy presents product filters, comparison, benefits and terms.
The prospect chooses a card before applying; displayed offers can vary.
exceptions: Current interactive comparison and personalized offer presentation were not inspected.
A recommendation or displayed maximum offer does not establish applicant eligibility.
checks.account_control_handoff: Etail proposal: show PERSONAL, HOUSEHOLD or SELLER context, membership plan, service eligibility and card format as separate choices before requesting a card.
checks.merchant_handoff: Etail proposal: card shopping creates no merchant acceptance agreement or Seller payout entitlement.
checks.etail_gap: The 90-task inventory starts at a card request. It lacks a product-selection decision and an explicit comparison of obligations, restrictions and usable benefits under Etail's own economics.
checks.acceptance_scenario: A prospect compares two permitted plans, sees exact fictional costs and repayment obligations, changes account context, and receives an updated explanation before any request exists.

checks.journey: Provide application information, review terms and accept a decision
normal_flow: US application help lists identity, contact and income information.
Indexed Personal-card copy distinguishes approval from choosing to accept the card.
exceptions: Required-field, consent, pending-information and acceptance-expiry screens were not inspected.
The researched Personal process cannot be assumed to apply identically to Small Business or Corporate programs.
checks.account_control_handoff: Etail proposal: identify the applicant, responsible adult and account; consent belongs to the appropriate person. An invitation, eligibility result or company approval does not grant spending.
checks.merchant_handoff: Etail proposal: no merchant can rely on application approval as a usable payment instrument.
checks.etail_gap: Specify product acceptance and its expiry/withdrawal policy separately from application consent. Keep all identity and decision demonstrations fictional; no real SSNs or credit checks.
checks.acceptance_scenario: An adult reviews a saved request, receives a simulated approval, leaves without accepting, and later sees whether the original offer is still valid. No card is represented as usable before all required steps complete.

checks.journey: Follow a pending application, decline and requested review
normal_flow: US support provides an application-status route distinct from existing-card service.
Earlier I19/I20 document decline explanations and review contact.
exceptions: Public sources do not expose a complete US pending taxonomy, missing-document deadline or guaranteed reconsideration outcome.
A request for review does not erase the original decision.
checks.account_control_handoff: Etail proposal: only the applicant and explicitly authorized sponsor/reviewer see the appropriate reasons and requested information.
checks.merchant_handoff: Etail proposal: pending or declined requests create no merchant-facing payment claim.
checks.etail_gap: Existing rows cover the headline tasks; complete the operational ownership, response deadline policy, abandoned-review handling and resolution notice without inventing Amex underwriting criteria.
checks.acceptance_scenario: A pending applicant learns who needs what information; a subsequent simulated decline remains visible when they request review, and the review ends with an explained unchanged or changed outcome.

checks.journey: Complete an employee application and company approval handoff
normal_flow: The earlier Corporate study documents separate applicant, company and issuer stages; see I05/I06 for market-specific routes.
exceptions: A company approval is not an issuer decision.
Current authenticated screens and every program's invitation expiry or resubmission rules remain unverified.
checks.account_control_handoff: Etail proposal: name the person responsible for the next step; preserve the selected Seller relationship and invalidate approval when material request details change.
checks.merchant_handoff: Etail proposal: an employer's internal approval cannot authorize a supplier charge before issuance and card-use eligibility.
checks.etail_gap: Retain the existing request journey and add operational handling for unavailable approvers, employee departure during review and corrected details. Guardian approval is an Etail adaptation, not a claim about Amex Corporate practice.
checks.acceptance_scenario: An employee completes their part, an approver changes, and the replacement approver sees the same current request. A later change of holder returns the request to review rather than issuing under stale approval.

checks.journey: Onboard the cardholder with their own access
normal_flow: US registration can create an online account or link a card to an existing one.
Additional-holder registration exposes that holder's card information.
exceptions: The public FAQ does not demonstrate failed linking, duplicate identities or recovery.
Do not infer Household-wide access from having a card.
checks.account_control_handoff: Etail proposal: invitation acceptance, person identity, card assignment, financial responsibility and management permission remain separately understandable.
checks.merchant_handoff: Etail proposal: the holder can see their transaction evidence; the merchant does not receive household relationships or unrelated account information.
checks.etail_gap: Review the complete first-login experience and mismatched invitation recovery. Explain who pays and who can change the card's controls before the holder's first purchase.
checks.acceptance_scenario: An invited holder signs in with their own identity, links only the intended fictional card and sees their purchases. A mismatched invitation gives a correction route without showing another person's information.

checks.journey: Deliver a new physical card and recover nonreceipt
normal_flow: The US general FAQ gives a 7–10 day expectation.
After receipt, the member confirms the card; if it has not arrived, replacement or phone help is available.
exceptions: This general timing differs from the Instant Card Number page and is not a universal guarantee.
The public FAQ does not describe every address correction, return-to-sender or shipment-loss stage.
checks.account_control_handoff: Etail proposal: distinguish approved, issued, delivery pending, receipt confirmed and eligible for use; address changes require the appropriate person's authority.
checks.merchant_handoff: Etail proposal: physical nonreceipt does not establish whether an independently supported digital method is available.
checks.etail_gap: Specify the service team's next action for simulated nonreceipt, invalid address and duplicate replacement requests. A sandbox shipping label must never imply real dispatch.
checks.acceptance_scenario: A fictional shipment passes its displayed estimate; the member sees a nonreceipt action and one linked replacement case, with the original request and delivery history preserved.

checks.journey: Confirm receipt, activate and attempt first use
normal_flow: US help documents confirmation online or in the mobile app with card details and security checks.
Mobile confirmation can use card proximity or manual entry.
exceptions: Public help does not disclose lockout limits or every failed-verification path.
Successful receipt confirmation does not establish that every future purchase will be approved.
checks.account_control_handoff: Etail proposal: explain which person can activate this product and whether a guardian must act; an administrator must not acquire cardholder spending authority by activating it.
checks.merchant_handoff: Etail proposal: first-use eligibility depends on active controls and available backing at purchase time.
checks.etail_gap: Replace the older Canada-only activation reference for the US benchmark. Include failed fictional verification, already-confirmed card and cancelled predecessor outcomes.
checks.acceptance_scenario: A permitted holder confirms a fictional card, repeats the action and sees the existing result. The first purchase separately explains approval or a current control restriction.

checks.journey: Use eligible digital details before the physical card arrives
normal_flow: Eligible US applicants retrieve Instant Card Number details after approval, online or from a welcome email.
The number matches the eventual physical card; digital-wallet use can begin before delivery.
exceptions: Eligibility depends on authentication; listed product exclusions apply.
Some merchants require the physical card, and full spending capacity may be unavailable before receipt confirmation.
checks.account_control_handoff: Etail proposal: display digital availability, physical fulfillment and activation distinctly; no fabricated usable payment number or unverified wallet support.
checks.merchant_handoff: Etail proposal: checkout must explain when the selected method requires physical presentation or cannot support the purchase.
checks.etail_gap: The existing catalog's transaction-specific virtual card is a different journey. Decide whether early digital availability is in Etail scope; otherwise retain it as an explicit comparison gap.
checks.acceptance_scenario: An eligible simulated card is digitally available while delivery remains pending. A physical-card-only checkout explains the restriction; receipt confirmation changes only the supported permissions.

checks.journey: Request a virtual payment and help the supplier use it
normal_flow: Earlier I07 documents transaction-bound virtual payments.
US support distinguishes buyer program help from supplier virtual-card inquiries.
exceptions: Public materials do not disclose every expired-number, partial-use, supplier rejection or cancellation procedure.
Do not treat Instant Card Number as a transaction-specific virtual card.
checks.account_control_handoff: Etail proposal: show the business purpose, intended payee, amount/date restrictions and people permitted to approve or obtain payment details.
checks.merchant_handoff: Etail proposal: supplier instructions and support must cover acceptance problems and payment matching, with a clear owner for unused or partially used payments.
checks.etail_gap: The catalog covers creation and controls; it lacks the supplier's receipt, rejection, unclaimed-payment and reconciliation handoff as a complete business journey.
checks.acceptance_scenario: A supplier cannot use an expired fictional virtual payment. The requester sees why, the support owner can choose a permitted correction, and no second payment is silently presented as successful.

checks.journey: Check planned spending and request changed capacity
normal_flow: US Check Spending Power assesses a planned purchase using account status at the request time.
A separate online route accepts Personal or Small Business limit-increase requests.
exceptions: No public promise reserves the checked amount for later.
The increase FAQ does not expose eligibility criteria, decision timing or decline categories.
checks.account_control_handoff: Etail proposal: distinguish account capacity from a holder's assigned spending limit and from actual available backing. Only the appropriate authority requests an increase.
checks.merchant_handoff: Etail proposal: a planning result is informational; the actual purchase receives its own current decision.
checks.etail_gap: Add a planning/check result and increase-request lifecycle if desired. A limit-change screen alone does not cover request, review, effective time and explanation.
checks.acceptance_scenario: A planned purchase looks possible, then another purchase consumes availability. The later checkout gives the current result; a pending increase request has not already raised the holder's usable amount.

checks.journey: Change holder controls, pause use and resume safely
normal_flow: Earlier I03/I08 document employee controls and consumer freeze behavior, including differences between products.
exceptions: A merchant-category alert is not proof of a purchase block.
Existing activity and permitted exceptions need separate explanation; no full private decision rule set was observed.
checks.account_control_handoff: Etail proposal: preview affected people, cards, period and remaining allowance; show who imposed each restriction and who can release it.
checks.merchant_handoff: Etail proposal: communicate the effective restriction without promising that every recurring or previously initiated transaction disappears.
checks.etail_gap: Complete the operational impact explanation and failure recovery. Etail's manual hierarchical freeze is an intentional deviation from Amex's documented consumer timing, not failed parity.
checks.acceptance_scenario: A guardian pauses a supervised card while a prior purchase is pending. The child cannot remove that restriction, the earlier purchase remains visible, and a later permitted refund is still handled.

checks.journey: Change the card product or plan without losing the history
normal_flow: US Offers terms document a consequence of moving to an ineligible card product: an existing offer may cease to qualify.
exceptions: A general US upgrade/downgrade request, decision, effective-date and fulfillment journey was not established from a current servicing guide.
Generic educational advice is not treated as Amex's operational procedure.
checks.account_control_handoff: Etail proposal: separately review membership plan changes, card format changes, new obligations and permissions; keep an owner for benefits questions.
checks.merchant_handoff: Etail proposal: explain any changed payment credentials or reward eligibility relevant to subsequent merchant purchases.
checks.etail_gap: Missing comparison journey. Define which Etail changes are allowed, their effective date, required consent and consequences; preserve membership-year cap and earned history.
checks.acceptance_scenario: An owner requests a permitted plan change and sees the exact effective date, benefits affected and unchanged historical obligations. The change does not restart the annual reward cap.

checks.journey: Replace a lost, stolen or damaged card and maintain continuity
normal_flow: US help invalidates a lost/stolen card immediately; a damaged card can remain usable pending replacement.
The account remains open. Shipment notification and existing merchant/wallet continuity are described.
exceptions: Without possession or online access, phone help may be required.
A merchant may request updated details; replacement is not cancellation of the merchant's subscription.
checks.account_control_handoff: Etail proposal: identify the reason, affected instrument, holder and authorized delivery address; preserve account responsibilities.
checks.merchant_handoff: Etail proposal: tell the member which saved methods require attention, while routing suspected fraud separately from a normal replacement.
checks.etail_gap: Expand the current replacement row with reason-specific old-card behavior, no-card/no-login support and merchant continuity. Do not imply real wallet updater support in the sandbox.
checks.acceptance_scenario: A lost fictional card is replaced once; its account and history remain. A recurring merchant request and a late refund can still be explained without restoring the old card for new ordinary purchases.

checks.journey: Renew an expiring card
normal_flow: US help describes automatic renewal to the address on file.
Consumer and Corporate renewal delivery expectations differ within the expiration month.
exceptions: Nonrenewal decisions and all delivery failures are not explained by this source.
Expiration is not the same request as user-reported loss or account closure.
checks.account_control_handoff: Etail proposal: give the right person a pre-expiry reminder and address-review opportunity; preserve controls, responsibility and membership history.
checks.merchant_handoff: Etail proposal: review continuity of stored payment methods and explain any action needed by the holder.
checks.etail_gap: Missing comparison journey. Define simulated expiring, renewal pending, renewed, nonrenewed and undelivered outcomes and their owners without promising automatic real issuance.
checks.acceptance_scenario: A fictional card approaches expiry while the mailing address is outdated. The holder sees the next step; expiry cannot erase outstanding purchases or falsely report that a replacement was delivered.

checks.journey: Offboard an employee and confirm card cancellation
normal_flow: A US Corporate administrator selects a card, supplies a cancellation reason and receives a tracking number.
The FAQ says individual cancellation is immediate.
exceptions: The published batch limit does not establish batch completion or partial-failure semantics.
The FAQ does not settle remaining expense, refund or repayment treatment.
checks.account_control_handoff: Etail proposal: revoke the departing person's access and card use as distinct operations; transfer unresolved business work to an authorized owner.
checks.merchant_handoff: Etail proposal: identify subscriptions, unsettled purchases and expected refunds that need business follow-up.
checks.etail_gap: The additional-card cancellation row needs employment offboarding context, responsible successor and evidence of completion. Household relationship changes require their own permitted authority.
checks.acceptance_scenario: An administrator offboards an employee with a pending purchase and unresolved expense. New use stops, the former employee's access ends, and finance retains a scoped record and next action.

checks.journey: Close an account or respond to an inactivity warning
normal_flow: US account closure is an assisted-service request; Corporate members may need the administrator.
Inactivity help promises warning and a way to keep the account open before possible closure.
exceptions: The public FAQs do not provide a complete final-statement, residual-balance or postclosure servicing sequence.
No fixed inactivity period is published here.
checks.account_control_handoff: Etail proposal: distinguish closing one card, one account and membership; preview affected holders and assign an owner to every remaining obligation or case.
checks.merchant_handoff: Etail proposal: settle or retain a clear route for delayed refunds, disputes and recurring-service follow-up.
checks.etail_gap: The catalog lacks full account closure and inactivity intervention. Local WORKFLOWS requires unresolved obligations, holds, refunds and cases to be handled; document the customer-facing consequences.
checks.acceptance_scenario: An owner requests closure with an outstanding refund and amount to repay. The screen explains what stops now, what remains open, who follows up and how statements/support remain accessible.

checks.journey: Understand billing balances and obtain the right statement
normal_flow: B05 distinguishes statement-related and current balances; I11 covers activity and statement access.
exceptions: A current balance is not a newly issued statement.
Recent activity, disputes and returned payments can require explanation; source-specific refresh wording is not a universal freshness promise.
checks.account_control_handoff: Etail proposal: show period, responsible party, amount due, pending purchases and authorized holder scope using Etail's own repayment rules.
checks.merchant_handoff: Etail proposal: transaction details provide the reference needed for a merchant return or billing inquiry without confusing it with the merchant's payout balance.
checks.etail_gap: The existing rows need a single explanation for why the statement and current total differ. Commercial daily full repayment and supervised funded spending are intentional Etail differences.
checks.acceptance_scenario: A payer sees a new purchase, a refund and a returned repayment after statement close and can explain the remaining obligation without interpreting pending purchases as a second debt.

checks.journey: Make, schedule, manage and stop repayment instructions
normal_flow: Earlier I12–I14 cover repayment, enrollment and eligible cancellation.
US AutoPay servicing additionally supports bank changes, pause/resume and stop.
exceptions: Stopping the recurring arrangement and cancelling one payment are different actions.
The settings FAQ does not establish the cutoff for instructions already processing.
checks.account_control_handoff: Etail proposal: show who may change a source versus execute a payment, the effective date and the obligation that remains due.
checks.merchant_handoff: Etail proposal: this is card-account repayment; it is not a merchant refund or a Seller payout.
checks.etail_gap: Enrollment is covered, but servicing an arrangement over time needs pause, resume, stop, source-change and in-progress instruction outcomes. Etail must define its own permitted schedule choices.
checks.acceptance_scenario: A payer pauses a fictional recurring instruction while today's payment is processing. The result states whether today's payment continues, what future instruction changed and what amount still needs attention.

checks.journey: Change the payment due date or statement cycle
normal_flow: The US FAQ offers an online due-date route for Credit Cards and chat for other listed products.
A change is conditional on eligibility.
exceptions: The effective cycle, effect on an existing scheduled payment and unavailable dates are not disclosed.
A due-date request is not already an approved extension.
checks.account_control_handoff: Etail proposal: route the request to the permitted payer/owner and display old date, proposed date and confirmed effective cycle.
checks.merchant_handoff: Etail proposal: changing a repayment schedule does not alter when a merchant's sale was completed.
checks.etail_gap: Missing comparison journey. Decide whether consumer schedules can change under Etail rules; commercial daily repayment cannot be replaced with Amex's product schedule.
checks.acceptance_scenario: A permitted payer requests a change after a statement is issued. They continue seeing the existing due date until a confirmed effective date explains which cycle and instruction are affected.

checks.journey: Recover a repayment returned by the funding institution
normal_flow: B04 documents returned-payment handling and conditional re-presentation.
exceptions: A previously applied payment is not proof that a later return cannot occur.
No Amex fee amount or retry policy is adopted for Etail.
checks.account_control_handoff: Etail proposal: explain the returned amount, resulting obligation, permitted next step and whether another collection attempt is expected.
checks.merchant_handoff: Etail proposal: a failed cardholder repayment is distinct from a merchant charge reversal; do not silently change an unrelated merchant sale.
checks.etail_gap: The existing returned status needs a complete recovery journey: assigned owner, member notice, corrected amount due, retry communication and hardship route.
checks.acceptance_scenario: A fictional repayment first appears applied, then is returned. The payer sees the linked correction and current amount due; choosing a replacement payment cannot create two unannounced attempts.

checks.journey: Follow a merchant return and request an issuer credit-balance refund
normal_flow: B03 supplies the billing-inquiry merchant contact route; B02 separately covers requesting return of an issuer credit balance.
exceptions: Merchant acknowledgement, posted purchase credit and cash returned by the issuer are different outcomes.
A merchant credit arriving during a dispute needs coordination; exact US postclosure refund handling was not established here.
checks.account_control_handoff: Etail proposal: identify whose money is being returned and any repayment amount still due; retain the original purchase and funding relationship.
checks.merchant_handoff: Etail proposal: the merchant owns the return decision and submission; issuer support owns an eligible account credit-balance refund request.
checks.etail_gap: A generic refund or dispute row does not cover negative/credit balances and postclosure return support. Define the consumer-facing separation and late-credit owner.
checks.acceptance_scenario: A merchant promises a refund before it posts, then the resulting credit exceeds the amount owed. The member sees each stage and a separate supported action for the excess, without claiming cash has already arrived.

checks.journey: Open a billing dispute, add evidence, follow progress and withdraw
normal_flow: B03/B07/B08 cover billing disputes and progress.
US help separately provides evidence submission and an action to close an ongoing dispute.
exceptions: Suspicious fraud uses the security route; merchant-first billing guidance must not delay a fraud report.
A closed case does not itself explain every financial adjustment, reopening right or final deadline.
checks.account_control_handoff: Etail proposal: show the permitted claimant, case reference, next actor, requested evidence and current obligation treatment without implying guaranteed reimbursement.
checks.merchant_handoff: Etail proposal: match merchant responses or credits to the original purchase and existing case; handle a late credit after withdrawal.
checks.etail_gap: Existing tasks need evidence receipt, awaiting-member/merchant work, missed-request handling, withdrawal consequences and final-resolution communication. These must be reviewed as one continuous case.
checks.acceptance_scenario: A member disputes a posted purchase, supplies requested fictional evidence, then receives a merchant credit and asks to withdraw. The case explains its actual status and linked financial outcome without duplicate reimbursement.

checks.journey: Seek hardship help and accessible servicing
normal_flow: B06 describes payment assistance and possible effects on card use.
US contacts offer cardholder assistance and relay support; I21 covers accessible statements.
exceptions: A request for help does not guarantee enrollment or terms.
The public FAQ does not disclose full eligibility decisions, plan-break consequences or reinstatement criteria.
checks.account_control_handoff: Etail proposal: explain the effect on the payer, additional holders and future use; offer an accessible assisted route without granting a helper unrelated account authority.
checks.merchant_handoff: Etail proposal: existing merchant claims and expected returns still need an assigned servicing owner.
checks.etail_gap: Hardship is not represented by ordinary repayment scheduling. Define scope and escalation for Etail; do not introduce Amex interest, lending or fee-relief products.
checks.acceptance_scenario: A payer reports difficulty and receives a safe support case with an accessible contact choice. Any simulated accommodation clearly states obligations and card-use effects before acceptance.

checks.journey: Raise a formal service complaint and receive a final response
normal_flow: UK procedures document a complaint reference, acknowledgement, progress communication, written determination and conditional external escalation.
The US directory establishes service contacts but not the same complete complaint process.
exceptions: UK insurance and other complaint routes differ; country-specific periods are not Etail promises.
US formal stages and response deadlines remain a research gap.
checks.account_control_handoff: Etail proposal: accept complaints from the affected person or properly authorized representative, name the owner and preserve communication preferences.
checks.merchant_handoff: Etail proposal: route merchant acceptance complaints to the merchant-service owner; a service complaint may link to, but must not replace, a transaction dispute.
checks.etail_gap: Missing comparison journey. Define receipt, triage, investigation, updates, decision, remedy and further-review options under Etail's actual operating scope.
checks.acceptance_scenario: A member complains about a mishandled replacement and also has a billing dispute. They receive one complaint reference and owner, can follow updates, and see a final response while the transaction case keeps its own outcome.
